response: {"text":"This research examined whether a person’s memory capacity stays the same compared with others when different kinds of information and presentation modes are used. Earlier work was unclear about whether memory span is a fixed personal trait (relative constancy) or changes with the type of material (absolute constancy). To test this, participants were given a series of recall tasks that involved ten distinct categories of items, each delivered through either a visual or an auditory channel. The goal was to see if each individual’s span remained proportionally stable within the group under both conditions, and also to determine if the overall size of the span stayed the same across materials. The findings showed that the maximum amount of information that can be held does vary with the nature of the material, supporting the view that absolute span is not constant. Consequently, the notion that memory span is universally general cannot be assumed."}
